verdict.rationale: cubic documents real programmatic surfaces: an Analytics API with an OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec, a versioned Members/organizations API with an interactive playground, and an official MCP server. The MCP server covers reading findings, requesting PR reviews, triaging issues, and managing subscriptions and seats. However, nothing in the evidence shows these surfaces cover everything the UI does, and many UI features appear only as UI, PR-comment or yaml-file workflows. missing for 10: documented API coverage for review settings (auto-approval, auto-fix), custom agents, codebase scans, AI wiki and integrations; an explicit API/UI parity statement; independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: cubic's MCP server lets your coding agent read review findings, look up codebase documentation, request PR reviews, triage PR or codebase scan issues
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
The Analytics API gives you PR-level data on how many issues were flagged, how many were fixed, how much AI code was authored, etc.
Each Members API endpoint page's markdown mirror embeds the full OpenAPI 3.1.0 YAML for that operation
